proved: For a physical cross block B and regularized determinant exponent q, aggregate k-minor mass E_k=e_k(BB^T) gives an explicit continuous-density bound when k>2q under the theorem's leverage scope.
At q=1,k=3 the constant is C3=(e/(6 sqrt(2))) Beta(1/6,1/12)=5.655763773... and the bound is C3 E3^(-1/6).
Removing a physical row multiplies the regularized determinant by exactly 1 minus its regularized leverage.
For exact rank three, average E3 across uniform coordinate cuts equals |det Lambda|^2 delta/64 for the partner Pluecker disjointness invariant delta.
A six-coordinate paired spectral frame with delta=1/8 has rank-three cross-cut mass E3=1/64 on every admissible split but leverage one on each side, refuting single-cut leverage selection.
